body.statement:
For the exact published one-proxy moment map \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{pub}}\), the observable class of \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\) is nonzero in \(\mathbb F[\mathbf m]/\mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}\), and \(R_{\mathrm{el}}=\beta W_2^{\mathrm{el}}-W_3^{\mathrm{el}}\) belongs to \(\mathcal I_{\leq3}\).  Consequently,
\[
\beta-\frac{W_3^{\mathrm{el}}}{W_2^{\mathrm{el}}}\in\mathcal I_{\leq3}^{(W)}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\mathcal I_{\leq3}K_{\mathrm{obs}}[\beta]
=\left\langle\beta-\frac{W_3^{\mathrm{el}}}{W_2^{\mathrm{el}}}\right\rangle.
\]
Thus every parameterized image point with \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\neq0\) has \(\beta=W_3^{\mathrm{el}}/W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\), and the generic full covariance-and-cubic fiber of \(\beta\) has degree one on this nonempty principal chart.  Extra roots of an individual retained eliminant are not additional common roots of the full localized ideal.  The conclusion does not classify the exceptional divisor \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}=0\) and does not assert identification on the entire unrestricted real parameter class.
body.proof_tex:
First we prove that the localization denominator is a nonzero observable class.  Consider the rational parameter point
\[
\gamma _1=\gamma _2=\gamma _3=u=\beta=1,
\qquad
\omega_j^{(2)}=\omega_j^{(3)}=1\quad(0\leq j\leq3).
\]
This step uses only the polynomial parameterization in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}published\text{-}mixing\text{-}map}\); no probabilistic positivity or support assertion is being made.  At this point
\[
\Lambda_{\mathrm{pub}}
=\begin{pmatrix}
1&1&0&0\\
2&1&1&0\\
3&1&1&1
\end{pmatrix},
\]
so the cubic equations in that definition give
\[
\mathbf c=(2,3,4,5,7,10,10,14,20,30).
\]
Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}linear\text{-}elimination\text{-}certificate}\) then yields
\[
N^{\mathrm{el}}
=\begin{pmatrix}
3\cdot7-4\cdot5\\
3\cdot4-2\cdot7\\
2\cdot5-3^2
\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}1\\-2\\1\end{pmatrix},
\]
and hence
\[
W_2^{\mathrm{el}}=5-20+14=-1,
\qquad
W_3^{\mathrm{el}}=7-28+20=-1.
\]
Every polynomial in \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}\) vanishes after every substitution from the parameterized image, by Definitions~\(\mathrm{def{:}full\text{-}published\text{-}moment\text{-}ideal}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}published\text{-}elimination\text{-}ideal}\).  The displayed evaluation therefore proves
\[
W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\notin\mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}.
\]
Thus its class is nonzero, and the principal chart on which it is invertible is nonempty.

We next establish the domain properties needed for passage to the observable function field.  Use the polynomial ring \(T\) and the substitution homomorphism \(\rho:\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pub}}\to T\) constructed in Proposition~\(\mathrm{prop{:}analytic\text{-}full\text{-}ideal\text{-}membership}\).  That proposition proves
\[
\ker\rho=\mathcal J_{\leq3}.
\]
The map \(\rho\) is surjective because it fixes every generator of \(T\).  The first isomorphism theorem and the fact that a polynomial ring over \(\mathbb F=\mathbb Q\) is an integral domain give
\[
\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pub}}/\mathcal J_{\leq3}\cong T,
\]
so \(\mathcal J_{\leq3}\) is prime.  A contraction of a prime ideal is prime; applying this directly to the two contractions in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}published\text{-}elimination\text{-}ideal}\) shows that \(\mathcal I_{\leq3}\) and \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}\) are prime.  Therefore
\[
A:=\mathbb F[\mathbf m]/\mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}
\]
is an integral domain and \(K_{\mathrm{obs}}=\operatorname{Frac}(A)\) is well defined.

Proposition~\(\mathrm{prop{:}analytic\text{-}full\text{-}ideal\text{-}membership}\) also proves
\[
R_{\mathrm{el}}=\beta W_2^{\mathrm{el}}-W_3^{\mathrm{el}}
\in\mathcal I_{\leq3}.
\]
Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}published\text{-}localization}\) inverts \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\).  Dividing the displayed ideal membership by that invertible element gives
\[
\beta-\frac{W_3^{\mathrm{el}}}{W_2^{\mathrm{el}}}
=\frac{R_{\mathrm{el}}}{W_2^{\mathrm{el}}}
\in\mathcal I_{\leq3}^{(W)}.
\]

It remains to show that this linear relation generates the full ideal after extension to \(K_{\mathrm{obs}}\).  Let \(\overline{\mathcal I}\) be the image of \(\mathcal I_{\leq3}\) in
\[
A[\beta]
=\mathbb F[\beta,\mathbf m]/\mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}.
\]
Because \(\mathcal I_{\leq3}\) is prime and contains \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}\), the ideal \(\overline{\mathcal I}\) is prime.  Moreover, the contraction identity
\[
\mathcal I_{\leq3}\cap\mathbb F[\mathbf m]=\mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}
\]
implies
\[
\overline{\mathcal I}\cap A=(0).
\]
Hence \(\overline{\mathcal I}\) is disjoint from the multiplicative set \(A\setminus\{0\}\), and its localization is a proper prime ideal
\[
\mathcal I_{\leq3}K_{\mathrm{obs}}[\beta]
\subsetneq K_{\mathrm{obs}}[\beta].
\]
The already proved relation and the nonzero class of \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\) give
\[
\left\langle\beta-\frac{W_3^{\mathrm{el}}}{W_2^{\mathrm{el}}}\right\rangle
\subseteq \mathcal I_{\leq3}K_{\mathrm{obs}}[\beta].
\]
The ideal on the left is maximal, because evaluation at \(\beta=W_3^{\mathrm{el}}/W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\) induces the field isomorphism
\[
K_{\mathrm{obs}}[\beta]\Big/
\left\langle\beta-\frac{W_3^{\mathrm{el}}}{W_2^{\mathrm{el}}}\right\rangle
\cong K_{\mathrm{obs}}.
\]
A proper ideal containing a maximal ideal must equal it.  Therefore
\[
\mathcal I_{\leq3}K_{\mathrm{obs}}[\beta]
=\left\langle\beta-\frac{W_3^{\mathrm{el}}}{W_2^{\mathrm{el}}}\right\rangle.
\]
Its quotient is one-dimensional over \(K_{\mathrm{obs}}\), which is exactly generic degree one for the \(\beta\)-fiber.  At every actual parameterized image point where \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\neq0\), the polynomial identity gives the pointwise recovery formula
\[
\beta=\frac{W_3^{\mathrm{el}}}{W_2^{\mathrm{el}}}.
\]
Finally, every individual retained eliminant becomes a multiple of the displayed linear generator over \(K_{\mathrm{obs}}\).  Zeros contributed by the multiplier are therefore zeros of that single eliminant, not additional common zeros of the full localized ideal.  None of these arguments applies after setting \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}=0\), so the exceptional divisor and its unrestricted real fibers remain unclassified, as stated.
body.justification: The theorem turns an independently derived cubic contraction into a precisely testable statement about the exact released full ideal and its observable localization.
body.gap: Tramontano et al. (2025), Theorem 3.6, reports generic nonidentification through order three; the unreported object tested here is the localized full-ideal relation \(\beta W_2^{\mathrm{el}}-W_3^{\mathrm{el}}=0\) under the exact published parameterization.
body.consumer: The result determines whether the one-proxy implementation may use a generic cubic effect chart on \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\ne0\), subject to the pinned replication gate.
